\smallskip
\footnotesize\emph{Note:} The two head changes are complementary.
Removing the parallel readout alone (C) is the worst variant for
accuracy, because without the residual the attention path is the only
route for drug information and carries it poorly; adding the residual
back (E) gives the best accuracy in the table. Together they cost
$0.0015$ PCC against the baseline (A vs.\ F). Faithfulness separates
the variants far more sharply than accuracy does: heads that retain a
bypass path sit at $0.02$--$0.06$, heads without one at $0.45$--$0.60$.
Comparing A$'$ with A isolates the pooling change, which accounts for
none of that movement. Single-seed runs; faithfulness varies by
${\sim}0.15$ between runs of one recipe, so small differences among
already-corrected variants are not interpreted.
\end{table*}
